newsitem.title: INDIA: Poor soybean arrivals hit Indian processing firms.
newsitem.headline: Poor soybean arrivals hit Indian processing firms.

text.p: Indian soybean crop arrivals have trickled to a minimum, forcing some soymeal processing firms to remain idle, traders said on Friday.
"Due to poor availability, some processing plants may close down next month," said a leading oilmeal broker.
"Only some big processing plants are getting raw material from markets and availability for small and medium plants (for processing) is very poor," said another broker.

Traders said soybean arrivals were around 8,000 tonnes per day in the central Indian markets, the hub of India's soybean processing industry. Last year, daily arrivals were around 20,000 tonnes at the same time.
Soybean was currently quoted at 10,700-11,100 rupees per tonne compared to 8,650-8,800 rupees same time last year.
Traders said export demand for India soymeal was dull. So far contracts have been signed to export nearly 1.45 million tonnes in 1996/97 (November-October).
Soymeal export prices were currently quoted at around $270-271 per tonne, against $218-220 at the same time last year.
